name: Digital Nomad / Remote Worker Visa

value.note: Defined as 3x the minimum income threshold for exemption from Italy's healthcare-contribution requirement. One Italian consulate (New York) states EUR 24,789; another (London) states EUR 25,500 for the same rule -- both are official esteri.it pages and this discrepancy is not resolved here.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires annual income of at least approximately EUR 24,789 (three times the minimum threshold for exemption from Italy's healthcare contribution) from remote self-employment for clients based outside Italy.
requirements.fix_path: Increase documented self-employment/remote income to the required threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a recognised bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree; an Italian-recognised regulated-profession licence; or at least 5 years' relevant professional experience (reduced to 3 years for ICT specialists, executives and senior managers).

Requires private health insurance covering medical expenses, hospitalisation, and repatriation with minimum coverage of EUR 30,000, valid for the full stay -- described by the source consulate as the single most common reason applications are rejected.
requirements.fix_path: Purchase qualifying health insurance before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a registered lease, rental contract, or property deed in the applicant's own name covering the full duration of the requested stay; hotel bookings or third-party hospitality letters are explicitly not accepted.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a registered lease or property deed before applying.

evidence_required.document: Degree certificate, professional licence, or documented 5 years' experience (3 for ICT/senior management)
Proof of annual income above the threshold (tax returns, client contracts)
Private health insurance certificate, minimum EUR 30,000 coverage
Registered lease, rental contract, or property deed covering the full stay

outcome.duration_length: 1-year permesso di soggiorno, renewable locally while employment, housing and insurance requirements are maintained

sources.title: Consulate General of Italy in New York (esteri.it) -- Digital Nomad / Remote Worker Visa: income, qualification, health insurance and accommodation requirements
Consulate General of Italy in London (esteri.it) -- Digital nomad visa (for self-employed only), citing a EUR 25,500 income threshold

notes: NEW ROUTE, added in this pass: Italy had 11 other routes built but no route for its Digital Nomad Visa, in force since the 4 April 2024 implementing decree under Article 27-quater of Legislative Decree 286/1998 (the same statute cited by esteri.it's New York page). LIVE DISCREPANCY, flagged rather than silently resolved: two different Italian consulates' own esteri.it pages give two different income figures for the same rule -- New York states EUR 24,789, London states EUR 25,500 -- both tier-1, both presumably restating the same year's statutory reference figure with some transcription or rounding difference between consulates; not resolved to a single number in this pass, and applicants should confirm the current figure with their own consulate before relying on either. family_can_join and family_can_work are deliberately omitted rather than guessed, and dual_citizenship_allowed is left null: no source fetched in this pass addressed dependants or dual citizenship specifically for this route, as distinct from Italy's general family-reunification rules. leads_to_pr (60 months) and leads_to_citizenship (120 months) are NOT confirmed by a source specific to this visa -- they are inferred from Italy's general rule that ordinary work-based residence permits count toward the 5-year EU long-term residence permit and the 10-year non-EU naturalisation-by-residence threshold (Testo Unico Immigrazione), absent any source found stating an explicit carve-out for this route (unlike Thailand's DTV or the UAE's Virtual Work Visa, where sources positively state no such path exists). This inference should be treated as the weakest-sourced claim in this file and revisited if a route-specific source surfaces. The 120-day processing time and the characterisation of the accommodation requirement as the leading rejection cause are both stated plainly by the source consulate.
